stem.en: Muscle tissue in your arm lets you lift a school bag. Which statement describes this tissue?

text.en: One very large cell that runs the whole length of the arm and does every job there.

feedback.en: One cell doing every job is how an amoeba lives. A tissue is a group of many cells.

text.en: A mix of all kinds of cells, such as skin, bone and nerve cells, each doing a different job.

feedback.en: These cells are not similar in structure and do not share one job, so together they are not one tissue.

text.en: Many identical cells that each move, digest food and carry messages on their own.

feedback.en: Each of these cells does every job, so there is no division of labour. The cells of a tissue share one specific job.

text.en: A group of similar cells that work together to make the arm move.

explanation.en: A tissue is a group of cells, similar in structure, that work together to perform a specific function. In muscle tissue the cells are similar to one another, and their shared job is movement.

hints.en: Check each choice for two things: are the cells similar, and do they share one job?
